metadata.case_name: LEE LUK PO v. SIN SZE T/A NGAI LUNG IRON WARE ENG

injuries.description: fracture of the spine at T12
source: fracture of the spine at T12
collapsed fracture at the anterio-superior aspect of T12 vertebra

injuries.description: the proximal interphalangeal joints of both middle fingers of both his hands were dislocated
injuries.body_part: proximal interphalangeal joints of both middle fingers
source: the proximal interphalangeal joints of both middle fingers of both his hands were dislocated

manifestations.description: intermittent pain which occurred daily, lasting some 10 to 20 minutes; he rated the pain to be in the region of 2 to 3 out of 10
reduced ability to lift heavy weights; he would suffer pain if he was lifting weights of up to 30 to 40 catties
residual pain over the thoracolumbar junction
there was no neurological deficit in his lower limbs

treatments_received: sent to the Accident & Emergency Department of the Pok Oi Hospital and then to Tuen Mun Hospital
fracture at T12 treated conservatively with thoracolumbarsacral orthosis
dislocation of the middle fingers managed with closed reduction and finger splintage
eight sessions of physiotherapy at the Kwong Wah Hospital
outpatient follow up at Tuen Mun Hospital and orthopaedics follow-up at Tseung Kwan O Hospital

losses.description: fracture of the T12 vertebra with residual reduction in height of less than 25 per cent and dislocation of the proximal interphalangeal joints of both middle fingers

reduced efficiency in resuming his duty as a metallic worker and welder on account of pain over his back when he had to climb, when performing heavy manual work, or on prolonged standing and bending of his back; endurance and power would also be moderately reduced and he might need intermittent breaks of 15 minutes after working for some two hours
